title: Disown
summary: DISOWN, verb transitive [dis and own.] 1. To deny; not to own; to refuse to acknowledge as belonging to ones self. A parent and hardly disown his child. An author will sometimes disown his writings. 2

inlines.v: DISOWN, verb transitive [dis and own.] 1. To deny; not to own; to refuse to acknowledge as belonging to ones self. A parent and hardly disown his child. An author will sometimes disown his writings. 2. To deny; not to allow. To disown a brothers better claim.
